scope.description: One five-voter history in one process: forty entries are committed on all five voters, the current leader and one follower are partitioned together and the leader appends a further forty entries that reach only that follower, so the pair holds an uncommitted suffix while the other three voters elect a new leader, commit twenty entries and publish a snapshot at an index below the suffix end. After healing, both minority members install that snapshot and become phantom holders. The same RequestVote, built from the stale follower's real cached claim and carrying the leadership-transfer flag, is then delivered to the phantom holder and to a majority voter whose cached state matches its snapshot.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced events are one partition of two voters from three, one clean retention of the minority suffix, and one explicit snapshot on the majority leader.

The stale candidate's claim is real (the follower really stores and caches the suffix it received from the deposed leader); the single supplied element is that its RequestVote carries the leadership-transfer flag, which is how a transferred-to or stale-transfer target campaigns and is what removes the known-leader rejection so the log test is reached.

Requests are delivered through another node's in-process transport with bounded retries, because a node's own transport has no peer entry for itself; retries only repeat the same single request payload.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

basis.prefix: The harness elects a leader in a five-voter cluster, commits forty entries, partitions the leader with one follower, drives forty further applies on the deposed leader so the pair shares an uncommitted suffix, waits for the pair to stop leading, waits for one of the remaining three to be the only stable leader, commits twenty entries there and forces Snapshot(), then heals the partition and waits until both minority members have installed the snapshot (their last snapshot index becomes non-zero). It records the phantom claim, snapshot and applied indexes on the phantom holder and on the second minority member, the consistent voter's claim/snapshot/applied, the leader's snapshot, and the candidate's real claim, then builds one RequestVote with term = the consistent voter's current term + 1, last log index/term from the stale follower's cached claim and the transfer flag, and delivers it to the phantom holder and to the consistent voter, recording the responses and the derived booleans.
basis.requirement: A voter's own log-completeness judgment for vote granting must not treat log entries the installed snapshot superseded as current, otherwise it can grant authority based on history it no longer holds.

comparisons.description: The phantom holder granted the vote request although its own installed snapshot already carries a newer term.
The voter whose cached state matches its snapshot rejected the same request, so the difference is the phantom claim rather than the request.
One identical request, two voters, different decisions in the same history.
The granted candidate's last log term is below the phantom holder's snapshot term, so the granted authority rests on entries the voter's snapshot superseded.
